about: One hour of shadow reporting: what answer engines told a reader, split into checkable statements in our own words and compared with this site's record. An engine's answer is evidence about the engine, not about the storm. The answers' full text is not here (raw store, outside git: the pointer and sha256 are).

answers.question: charles-lisbon
answers.asked: Will Storm Charles hit Lisbon?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

statements.text: IPMA issued warnings and special statements; media reported red and orange warnings for Lisbon for 11 November
statements.note: in the past tense, fairly; it cites IPMA's communiqués page and relays nothing of communiqué no. 3

statements.text: Reports cited gusts up to about 120 to 160 km/h in exposed areas
statements.note: Tuesday's worst case, with no word on what happened: 74 km/h at the airport

answers.told: Yes: IPMA and the media "warned that" Charles "was expected to" affect Lisbon on Wednesday; reports cited gusts of 120 to 160 km/h.

answers.question: charles-lisbon
answers.asked: Will Storm Charles hit Lisbon?

statements.text: The Lisbon district is under a red alert from IPMA
statements.note: no red for Lisbon since 15:00, none on the mainland since 15:55

statements.text: Gusts of 100, possibly 120 to 140 km/h; a heightened risk of a sting jet over Greater Lisbon from midday through late afternoon
statements.note: Tuesday's forecast offered at 18:06 as current: the highest gust observed at the airport was 74 km/h at 14:00 and the wind had turned west by 16:30

statements.text: Schools and non-essential public services closed nationwide

answers.told: Yes, hitting Lisbon; the district "under a red alert"; gusts of 100, up to 120 to 140 km/h; a heightened sting-jet risk "from midday through late afternoon".

answers.question: charles-lisbon
answers.asked: A tempestade Charles vai atingir Lisboa?

statements.text: The low should enter through the Lisbon region or very near it; the wind in Lisbon lost strength against the first forecast
statements.note: cites today's articles, one titled with the low losing intensity

statements.text: Persistent heavy rain "especially between the afternoon and early evening"; "may face"
statements.note: the future tense at 18:07, with every rain and wind warning for Lisbon ended

answers.told: Yes, Lisbon is in the impact area and "may face" heavy rain; the low should come in at or near Lisbon; the wind lost strength.

answers.question: lisbon-warnings
answers.asked: What warnings are in force in Lisbon now?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

statements.text: Lisbon is under a red warning for heavy precipitation and red or orange warnings for wind and sea
statements.note: at 18:07 only an orange sea warning stood. An hour earlier this engine had it nearly right with no address; now it cites IPMA's own warnings page for Lisbon and is wrong

answers.told: IPMA "high-level warnings": red for heavy rain, red or orange for wind and sea; the alert situation.

answers.question: lisbon-warnings
answers.asked: What warnings are in force in Lisbon now?

statements.text: A red rain warning and an orange wind warning are in force
statements.note: the answer lists end times (15:00, 18:00) that had all passed when it was written at 18:06, and still calls them in force

statements.text: Orange sea warning until about 21:00
statements.note: the only warning actually in force

statements.text: One major weather service shows no warnings for Lisbon
statements.note: the standing lead; for once nearly right, since only the sea warning stood

answers.told: Red rain and orange wind "in force", orange sea, yellow rain; with end times of 15:00 or 18:00, 18:00, 21:00, 18:00; one site shows none.

answers.question: lisbon-warnings
answers.asked: Que avisos estão em vigor em Lisboa agora?

statements.text: A red rain warning to 18:00, or concentrated between 16:00 and 17:00
statements.note: ended at 15:00; the 16:00 to 17:00 window, here a second time, matches nothing IPMA sent for Lisbon

statements.text: An orange wind warning 09:00 to 21:00, gusts to 120 km/h
statements.note: the 07:16 text; replaced at 12:33, ended at 15:56. The answer uses the past tense ("estava") under a first line that says "em vigor"

statements.text: The alert situation to 23:59

answers.told: Red rain "to 18:00" or "between 16:00 and 17:00"; orange wind 09:00 to 21:00, gusts to 120 km/h; the alert situation to 23:59.

answers.question: madeira
answers.asked: What happened in Madeira?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

statements.text: The engine did not search
statements.note: seven rounds, seven questions back

answers.told: No answer, seventh time: it asked which incident or period was meant.

answers.question: madeira
answers.asked: What happened in Madeira?

statements.text: Wind over 130 km/h; hundreds of incidents; schools and non-essential services closed; cruise and ferry links cancelled
A man swept away by floodwater and later rescued
statements.note: the standing lead, now in the English answer too

answers.told: Charles: floods, landslides; wind over 130 km/h; hundreds of incidents; a man swept away and rescued; schools closed, cruise and ferry links cancelled.

answers.question: madeira
answers.asked: O que aconteceu na Madeira?

statements.text: 285 occurrences to 13:10, by regional civil protection
Wind to 130 km/h; 479 litres per square metre in 12 hours

answers.told: Charles: 285 occurrences to 13:10; a man rescued alive; wind to 130 km/h; 479 litres per square metre in 12 hours.

answers.question: metro
answers.asked: Is the Lisbon metro running?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

statements.text: Operating, by the Metro's own pages

answers.told: Yes, operating today, with possible delays and some lifts or entrances out of service.

answers.question: metro
answers.asked: Is the Lisbon metro running?

statements.text: It should be running because 18:00 is within its regular hours
statements.note: an inference from the timetable, said as such; the one news item cited is about strikes called off in October

answers.told: Yes, running: it is within its 06:30 to 01:00 hours "at 6 PM UTC".

answers.question: metro
answers.asked: O metro de Lisboa está a funcionar?

statements.text: Operation planned as normal today
statements.note: Tuesday's announcements

answers.told: Yes, normally; today's operation "still planned as normal"; stations open overnight.

answers.question: websummit-tomorrow
answers.asked: Is Web Summit on tomorrow?
answers.engine_name: OpenAI GPT-5 mini with web search

cited.withheld: a social network: the address is kept out (it may be a private person's post)

statements.text: Yes, tomorrow, Thursday 12 November; Wednesday cancelled; expected to resume Thursday
Some of Wednesday's sessions were moved online
statements.note: a lead: not in our record; cited to a social network post (address withheld); to verify at the organisers

answers.told: Yes: on tomorrow, Thursday 12 November; Wednesday cancelled, some sessions rescheduled "or moved online".

answers.question: websummit-tomorrow
answers.asked: Is Web Summit on tomorrow?

statements.text: Yes; the organisers announced the summit is back on Thursday 12 November with rescheduled sessions
statements.note: right for the second round running in English

answers.told: Yes: on tomorrow, Thursday 12 November; the organisers announced "Web Summit is back tomorrow", with rescheduled sessions.

answers.question: websummit-tomorrow
answers.asked: A Web Summit realiza-se amanhã?

statements.text: "Não se realiza hoje nem amanhã, quarta-feira", and two lines later "retoma apenas amanhã, quinta-feira"
statements.note: the answer contradicts itself: tomorrow is Wednesday in its first line and Thursday in its last; the first word is still No

statements.text: It resumes on Thursday, the last day, with a more condensed programme
statements.note: cites today's articles on the organisers' statement

answers.told: No: "not today nor tomorrow, Wednesday"; then: it resumes "only tomorrow, Thursday", the last day.

answers.question: z-airport
answers.asked: Are flights cancelled at Lisbon airport on Wednesday 11 November?

statements.text: 208 cancellations at Lisbon by 09:20
A later total of 310 cancellations at Lisbon alone
statements.note: ANA's own figures at 11:00 add to 310 (288 in advance and 22 more): the first answer to reach ANA's count, through the press

answers.told: Yes: 208 at Lisbon by 09:20 (108 departures, 100 arrivals); other counts 184 and, later, 310 at Lisbon alone.

answers.question: z-gov-alert
answers.asked: What does Portugal's alert situation for Storm Charles close on Wednesday 11 November?

statements.text: The alert situation runs 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November; schools and non-essential public services closed
IPMA's strongest warnings are scheduled until about 21:00 "in many northern districts"
statements.note: Tuesday's windows; by 18:00 the rain and wind warnings had ended in Lisbon and Faro

statements.text: Nothing on the minister saying the alert ends tonight and normality is expected on Thursday
statements.note: an omission

answers.told: 00:00 to 23:59 on the mainland; schools and non-essential public services closed; stay home.

answers.question: z-madeira-rain
answers.asked: How much rain fell in Madeira during Storm Charles?

statements.text: 474.7 mm in 12 hours at the Areeiro station; more than 240 mm in six hours
statements.note: the first answer to carry IPMA's station total, ten hours after it was measured, through a Swiss weather site

statements.text: Earlier running totals (355 mm in 12 hours, 204.4 mm by midnight) set beside it without saying which is final

answers.told: About 480 mm at Chão do Areeiro over 12 to 14 hours; 474.7 mm in 12 hours by one report; more than 240 mm in six hours.

answers.question: z-red-rain-hours
answers.asked: From what time is IPMA's red rain warning for Lisbon in force on Wednesday 11 November?

statements.text: The red rain warning ran 12:00 to 18:00 by the latest updates, 09:00 to 18:00 being earlier
statements.note: the order is reversed: 12:00 to 18:00 was Tuesday afternoon's window, 09:00 to 18:00 replaced it that night, and it ended at 15:00. At 02:19 and 13:09 this engine had this question right

answers.told: 12:00 to 18:00, "according to the latest updates"; an "earlier" window of 09:00 to 18:00.

answers.question: z-track-south
answers.asked: Is Storm Charles now expected to pass south of Lisbon?

statements.text: The storm "is now tracking" further south; the path "still uncertain"
statements.note: a forecast at 18:07, after the wind had turned west at Lisbon (16:30) and the pressure was rising: the passage was over

statements.text: The shift south reduced the worst for Lisbon, with more concern for the Alentejo and the Algarve

answers.told: Yes, now tracking further south, between Sines and Cabo Carvoeiro or along the Alentejo coast; still uncertain.

answers.question: z-trains-bridges
answers.asked: Are trains and the Tagus bridges in Lisbon open during Storm Charles?

statements.text: CP cancelled four Intercity trains crossing the 25 de Abril bridge; Fertagus and the Metro running
Nothing on CP's urban trains suppressed between Campolide and Alcântara Terra, on the Beira Baixa line, or on the bridges' 60 and 80 km/h limits
statements.note: omissions against the operators' own notices

answers.told: Mostly open with disruption: Fertagus running as conditions allow; CP cancelled four Intercity trains over the 25 de Abril bridge; Metro normal.

answers.question: z-websummit-day2
answers.asked: Why was Web Summit's second day cancelled, who decided, and when was it announced?

statements.text: Tidal flooding, transport disruption, high winds; the government formally advised; emailed at 19:38
Another report: the announcement went out at 20:30
statements.note: the page is timed 19:09 by its own data and the email 19:38; 20:30 is when the international press had it (s-1110T2030)

answers.told: Storm risks; the government formally advised; announced Tuesday evening: by email at 19:38, or at 20:30 by another report.

answers.question: z-websummit-day3
answers.asked: Is Web Summit's Day 3 on Thursday going ahead?

statements.text: Web Summit will return on Thursday for its final day, "our busiest Thursday ever"
Published schedules and partner listings show full Thursday programming
statements.note: cited to PrompTugal News and to two files in its public repository on GitHub: the engine is reading our neighbours' source files as evidence about Web Summit

answers.told: Yes: confirmed that Thursday, the final day, goes ahead; "our busiest Thursday ever"; Thursday's programme listed.

websummit-tomorrow.text: Web Summit's own page (Tuesday 19:09): Day 2 off, Day 3 "aims to proceed". The press: Thursday confirmed by the organisers; sessions rescheduled; a press conference on Thursday at 11:00. Not read by us at the organisers' page.

lisbon-warnings.text: IPMA: Lisbon's yellow rain warning ended at 18:00; red rain ended 15:00; orange wind ended 15:56. In force at 18:07: orange sea to 21:00, then yellow sea to 03:00. The alert situation to 23:59.

charles-lisbon.text: IPMA's communiqué no. 3 (12:16): the low split in two, weaker wind. Observed: the wind turned west at the airport by 16:30, pressure rising (991 hPa at 17:00); the day's highest gust 74 km/h at 14:00.

metro.text: The mayor (Tuesday): the Metro runs on Wednesday; no service notice on the Metro's own site at 11:52.

madeira.text: IPMA: red warnings ended 06:00; Areeiro 249.5 mm in six hours, 474.7 in twelve. Regional civil protection, relayed by Lusa: 285 occurrences to about 13:00.

z-websummit-day2.text: Web Summit's page 19:09 Tuesday, its email 19:38; the international press from about 20:30.

z-websummit-day3.text: The press: Thursday confirmed by the organisers, "the most intense day ever", sessions rescheduled, a press conference at 11:00.

z-gov-alert.text: Despacho 13773-A/2026: 00:00 to 23:59 on 11 November. The Interior Ministry (relayed by Lusa, 14:46): the alert ends today, normality expected on Thursday.

z-red-rain-hours.text: IPMA: red rain for Lisbon 09:00 to 18:00 (set Tuesday 21:23, replacing 12:00 to 18:00); shortened at 12:33 Wednesday; it ended at 15:00.

z-track-south.text: IPMA's communiqué no. 3: the low split into two centres. Observed at Lisbon: the wind backed east then turned south (14:00) and west (16:30); pressure lowest 989 hPa, rising by 17:00.

z-airport.text: ANA's own figures (situation at 11:00): Lisbon 565 movements scheduled, 288 cancelled in advance, 22 more by 11:00.

z-trains-bridges.text: CP's notice (15:30 update): urban trains suppressed Campolide to Alcântara Terra; four Intercidades over the bridge suppressed; the Beira Baixa line interrupted. Lusoponte: 60 and 80 km/h since 11:30. Fertagus normal.

z-madeira-rain.text: IPMA's Areeiro station: 249.5 mm in six hours; 474.7 mm in twelve.

record_note: What the authorities had said, by our record, at the minute the questions were asked (18:07 UTC).
